purpose: Conservative color-correction workflow and creative grade starting points for project video types.

deliveryAssumption.note: Do not label output BT.709 without first interpreting and converting the source correctly. HDR and log workflows require explicit transforms not defined by these SDR presets.

correctionWorkflow.goal: Read source primaries, transfer, matrix, range, bit depth, and camera profile before applying a look.
Convert supported source material into the working SDR color space with an explicit colorspace or zscale transform when needed.
checks: skin and neutral objects remain plausible

correctionWorkflow.goal: Set believable black, midtone, highlight, and neutral color before style.
checks: white objects are neutral when appropriate
sky and food highlight detail survives

correctionWorkflow.goal: Make adjacent shots feel as though they belong in one sequence.
Apply one selected look at restrained strength, adjusting per shot when necessary.
Inspect encoded output rather than trusting only filter parameters.

guardrails: A preset is a starting point, not a replacement for per-shot correction.
Do not apply a creative LUT before normalizing mismatched source footage.
Protect skin tones, food identity, sky gradients, and reflective highlights.
Prefer small changes across several controls over one extreme saturation or contrast operation.
Avoid sharpening noisy or highly compressed action-camera footage before denoising and scaling decisions are complete.
Render a short representative sample before grading the full timeline.

grades.name: Neutral Cinematic
grades.intent: Natural color with slightly firmer contrast and restrained saturation, suitable as the safest default.

grades.name: Warm Travel
grades.intent: A welcoming sunlit look for streets, beaches, people, and travel memories without turning neutrals orange.

grades.name: Subtle Teal and Orange
grades.intent: Cooler shadows and warmer highlights create separation for action and city footage while keeping the effect secondary to subject color.
avoid: using on every daylight beach shot

grades.name: Clean Vibrant
grades.intent: Bright, clear, and legible color for products, tutorials, graphics, gaming, and general social content.

grades.name: Natural Action
grades.intent: Controlled action-camera footage with readable road, sky, landscape, and machine detail rather than an exaggerated action-sports look.
avoid: grade changes caused by automatic exposure shifts

grades.name: Clean Talking Head
grades.intent: Consistent skin, neutral background color, and gentle contrast for speech-led footage.
avoid: different white balance between jump cuts

grades.name: Clean Food
grades.intent: Warm-neutral presentation that emphasizes texture and freshness while preserving the real identity of ingredients.

grades.name: Vintage Film
grades.intent: A nostalgic lower-saturation look with softened contrast, optional grain, and restrained vignette.

ffmpegCapabilities.lutRule: Treat a LUT as one creative transform in a controlled color pipeline. Record LUT path, file hash, expected input color space, and strength method.
ffmpegCapabilities.validationRule: Render representative samples and inspect image content; a syntactically valid filter graph does not prove a good grade.

supports: availability and behavior of FFmpeg color, LUT, curve, vignette, sharpen, denoise, and signal-analysis filters
